newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Three Israeli banks rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Three Israeli banks rated a buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers rated three Israeli banks a buy but refrained from making an investment recommendation on a fourth bank in a report released on Sunday.

The report, by analyst Mathew Czepliewicz, noted that Bank Leumi and Bank Hapoalim had been instructed by the Israeli government to pay out dividends on capital gains arising from the reduction or sale of non-bank holdings.
"We interpret this to mean that the banks are expected to make full payouts of these gains," the report said.
"If this interpretation is correct, Bank Leumi shareholders would book a supplemental yield of 5.8 percent and Bank Hapoalim shareholders a booster yield of 1.6 percent," it said.
Czepliewicz also retained a buy on First International Bank of Israel, although it will not be be making any special payout.

Salomon cited the possible effects of Israel Discount Bank's fourth-quarter debt-provision in continuing to withhold its recommendation. He noted that Discount would not be paying any special dividend.

"(Discount) was already looking at the weakest 1996 estimated earnings per share growth in the sector, a reflection in part of investor concerns about the bank's loan book," the Salomon report said, citing the bank's exposure to the property market.

Discount said on Sunday it would delay until April a secondary offering of shares and warrants originally scheduled for this month after it concluded it could not provide detailed enough financial figures for the fourth quarter to meet Securities Authority requirements.
